title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for history of right lung malignancy.

HPI
The patient is a 57-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up regarding a history of cancer in the right lung. The primary malignancy was surgically removed and treated several years ago. He reports feeling well and denies any new respiratory symptoms, chest pain, or persistent cough. He states he has had no issues since the completion of his previous treatment plan. He is here today primarily for surveillance and to confirm that there is no evidence of recurrence at the primary site. He reports no systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss or night sweats.

Medication List
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Review of Systems
The patient reports no recent cough, shortness of breath, or chest pain. He denies fever, chills, or night sweats. He denies any recent weight loss or changes in appetite. He denies any new-onset localized pain or neurological changes.

Social History
The patient is a non-smoker and reports moderate alcohol consumption on weekends only. He works full-time in a construction management role and lives with his wife and two children.

Family History
Father had a history of hypertension. Mother had a history of type 2 diabetes. No family history of malignancy is reported.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on room air

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.5 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 210 x 10^9/L
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezing or rales noted.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs or gallops.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, and non-distended.
Musculoskeletal: No localized edema or tenderness noted.

Assessment
The patient is a 57-year-old male with a history of malignancy in the right lung. Clinical evaluation and history indicate that the primary tumor was successfully treated years ago. Currently, there is no evidence of recurrence at the primary site. The patient remains stable and asymptomatic.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Continue routine surveillance.
3. Follow up in six months for a repeat physical examination and review of imaging.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: The right lung cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.118 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
